messages:
anj: FYI - noticed correlation between high p95 latency and mixed-dim embedding requests. prebatcher currently coalesces by arrival window which drives up compute for tiny items when large dims are present.

pete: yeah saw that in the latency heatmap. small docs get stuck behind a 1024-dim item and then take a slow path. throughput good but tail suffers.

maya: ops tradeoff: either split mixed-dim into separate sub-batches (more batches == more kernel invocations) or keep coalescing and accept inefficient CPU usage. both affect quotas/units in different ways.

ops-lee: question: if we split we can compute per-item units accurately which helps billing fairness. however splitting increases scheduling overhead and may raise 95th. need telemetry to measure net cost.

pm-hugo: customers care about predictable unit billing. if we can offer a tenant-level policy toggle (split-mixed-dims: true/false) that would be great UX-wise. default should be conservative.

console-bot: created ticket #ENG-1298 and dashboard stub for MixedDim split policy metrics.

anj: proposal sketch: router adds policy header X-Embed-Split: auto|always|never. default=auto. semantics:
- always: split items in the ingress into separate sub-batches by dim
- never: keep current coalesce behavior
- auto: heuristics: if mixed-dim ratio > 0.5 and avg small-item latency > threshold then split else coalesce

pete: implementation notes: we should avoid per-request heavy calculations. heuristics must be cheap (count distinct dims up to N, ratio calc). also respect 'prefer-low-latency' client header to override.

maya: + add console-level per-tenant override so sales/CS can set policy for specific customers. also expose estimated impact prior to flipping (computed from sampled traces).

ops-lee: telemetry plan: emit metrics per-tenant/sample: mixed_dim_count, subbatch_count, kernel_invocations, old_est_units, new_est_units, p95_latency_delta. sample 0.5% to start.

sre-ivy: add safety: if enabling 'always' causes kernel_invocations spike above X per-second, auto-fall back to 'auto' for that tenant and send alert. also add circuit to avoid cascading high CPU across nodes.

pm-hugo: UX notes: console toggle with inline estimate UI: "Projected monthly delta: +X% CPU, -Y% billed units". This helps sales conversations. Include a small FAQ item.

anj: rollout plan: backend-only feature flag first. Steps:
1) router accepts X-Embed-Split and logs decision with trace tag
2) runtime implements efficient split-on-dim path (fast path for homogeneous dims stays)
3) start sampling 0.5% tenants with 'always' to collect cost/latency deltas
4) expose dashboard cards and per-tenant toggle in Console behind feature flag
5) opt-in beta for selected customers

pete: curious edgecases: what about mixed dims where dims differ slightly (e.g., 256 vs 320) from quantized models? consider group-by-bucket instead of strict equality.

maya: agree. group dims by bucket ranges: small: <=256, med: 257-768, large: >768. grouping reduces explosion of sub-batches. add config for buckets.

ops-lee: security/observability: ensure we don't log full client payloads. only emit dims and counts. mask everything else.

sre-ivy: also add per-node backpressure metric when subbatching increases memory pressure. alert if memory > 75% for 2-min window.

pm-hugo: can we show a "what-if" simulator in console that runs sampled traces through split-vs-coalesce and shows estimated billing/latency delta?

console-bot: added "what-if" simulator task to #ENG-1298. owners: @pete, @maya.

anj: open questions: default for new tenants? my leaning: default=auto with small-sample always-on to collect better baseline.

maya: +1. also expose logs so customers can see which requests were split (by trace id) for troubleshooting.

pete: timeline: dev PRs this week, canary deploy next Tue, sampling ramp over 2 weeks, console UI after telemetry stabilizes.

sre-ivy: put guardrails on canary: allow only 5 canary tenants at a time for the "always" policy.

ops-lee: will add runbook for CS: steps to flip tenant policy, how to interpret dashboard, rollback steps.

anj: ok assigning tasks in ticket. if anyone has strong objections ping me. otherwise proceed. :rocket:
